examShortTricks: Trick 1: The play's charm is RECOGNITION: two elderly ex-sweeteners meet as strangers feeding birds and gradually recognise each other — the gradual reveal structure is the answer.
Trick 2: Vanity and age: each pretends to be younger and blames the other for not recognising them — the comic irony of mutual self-deception.
Trick 3: The crumbs and the bench: small props carry nostalgia — link one prop to the theme of lost love and time.
practiceQuestions: Q. How do Dona Laura and Don Gonzalo conceal their identities at first? (2 marks) — each invents a younger self and a fictional past, afraid of ridicule.
Q. What is the theme of the play? (2 marks) — ageing, vanity and the sweet persistence of first love.
keyPoints: Former lovers meet as old strangers — neither recognises the other at first.
Humour comes from vanity: both invent glamorous versions of their past.
